title: dockato: fixed dihedral angle (DIH groups)
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. With dminrr = dmaxrr the new bond gets a fixed dihedral and a DIH rotational group instead of a ROT group.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: The building block `WaterMolecule.ato` of EPSR-test: one water molecule (O1, H1, H1; O-H 0.976 Å, H-H 1.54 Å, SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charges [@berendsen1987]) in a 14.42 Å box at 300 K. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. As in ex80 the water units are joined by O-O bonds (docking H1 on docked O1); the dihedral reference atoms are `H1` on both sides.
inputs: All parameters on the command line: run 1 `... 4 10 WaterMolecule.ato O1 H1 H1 120 120 yes waterdih` (fixed 120°, overlaps allowed, 4 molecules); run 2 fixed 75° with overlap factor 0.8, 4 molecules (`waterdih2`).
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. `waterdih.ato`: 7 atoms (all 4 dockings) and 4 DIH groups; `waterdih2.ato`: 5 atoms and 2 DIH groups, i.e. 2 of 4 placements accepted by the 0.8 overlap test. The case exercises the DIH group output of `moloutc` (DIH writing was added to the port's `moloutc` for this).
